title: Share vs NTFS Permissions in Windows

scenes.line1: Why can't users write to a share?
scenes.say: Ever seen a user with full control on a shared folder, but they still can't write files? Let's break down why that happens.
Windows uses two layers: share permissions, which control access over the network, and NTFS permissions, which control everything on the folder itself.

scenes.label: Restrictive
scenes.sub: Access is limited by the most restrictive permission.
scenes.say: Here's the trick: the most restrictive permission always wins. If one blocks write, you can't write, no matter what the other says.

scenes.title: See Permissions
scenes.say: To check, use PowerShell to view both share and NTFS permissions. Or, use the folder's properties and check the Effective Access tab.

scenes.question: User has Full Control on share but can't write?
scenes.right: NTFS permissions are blocking write. Effective access is the most restrictive of both.
scenes.say: Here's a classic interview trap: a user has full control on the share, but can't write. It's almost always because NTFS permissions are blocking them.
